AgentRunStateV1.description:
Per-run agent state.

The relation fields below are a **read-only permission snapshot**, projected
from the relation ledger at each policy evaluation — the same pattern as
`permission_snapshot`. They are never the authority for relation state.

Treating them as authoritative fails in two ways. Two concurrent runs on one
asset would hold independent relation sets with no reconciliation, so
whichever wrote last would win. Worse, a long-running run would keep
authorizing detail reads from a set projected before the user corrected a
bound asset — the exact stale access GRAG-16 exists to catch. Re-projecting
at each evaluation keeps the permission decision tied to current canonical
state.
AgentRunStateV1.title: AgentRunStateV1

ConfirmedAssetRelationV1.description:
A durable bilateral relation created by an explicit confirmation.

`relation_id` is distinct from `source_candidate_id`: the relation is a new
durable object, while the candidate is the proposal it came from. Ticket 07
checks the source candidate against the run's candidate set, which preserves
the original intent — nothing can be confirmed which was never proposed —
without requiring the two identifiers to be the same value.
ConfirmedAssetRelationV1.title: ConfirmedAssetRelationV1

ConfirmedRelatedEvidenceArguments.description:
Bounded detail read for an already-confirmed relation.

The free-text query is removed here too, but it is **not** replaced by a
discovery intent. The readable set is computed from the exact confirmed
relation, its bindings, and the validated mapping and boundary package, so
any remaining tunable would mean one confirmation could read different
things on different calls — precisely what "one confirmation unlocks one
asset's bounded evidence" exists to prevent.
ConfirmedRelatedEvidenceArguments.title: ConfirmedRelatedEvidenceArguments

ConfirmedRelationBinding.description: One exact user-confirmed relation-to-asset access binding.
ConfirmedRelationBinding.title: ConfirmedRelationBinding

CriticalMomentMapV1.description: M2 artifact bound to one accepted M1 version and its source statements.
CriticalMomentMapV1.title: CriticalMomentMapV1

DecisionEvidenceLedgerV1.description: Editable M3 artifact bound to one exact accepted M2 state.
DecisionEvidenceLedgerV1.title: DecisionEvidenceLedgerV1

DiscoveryFailureClass.description:
Safe failure classes retained for audit.

None of these is reusable as a semantic result. Reusing one would let a
five-minute outage permanently erase a relation that may well exist.
DiscoveryFailureClass.title: DiscoveryFailureClass

DiscoveryOutcome.description:
Discriminated outcomes of one cross-asset discovery request.

`NO_MATCH` is a semantic claim and is cached; `TECHNICAL_FAILURE` is not.
Collapsing the two would make a temporary outage indistinguishable from a
proven absence of relation, and the cache would then preserve the outage
permanently.
DiscoveryOutcome.title: DiscoveryOutcome

ExperienceAssetV1.description: Complete canonical JSON snapshot stored for each immutable version.
ExperienceAssetV1.title: ExperienceAssetV1

ExperienceBriefV1.description: Typed payload stored inside the canonical M1 artifact envelope.
ExperienceBriefV1.title: ExperienceBriefV1

InsightBoundaryMapV1.description: Editable M4 artifact bound to one exact accepted M3 state.
InsightBoundaryMapV1.title: InsightBoundaryMapV1

InsightEntryV1.description: One lesson together with the boundary that makes it safe to reuse.
InsightEntryV1.title: InsightEntryV1

InsightStatementV1.description:
One role-bearing statement inside an insight entry.

A statement is either grounded in canonical M3 evidence or explicitly marked
as a visible gap. There is no third state: an ungrounded statement that does
not declare itself a gap renders identically to a supported one, and the
reader has no signal that something is missing.
InsightStatementV1.title: InsightStatementV1

KnowledgeCardReadinessRecordV1.description:
Sidecar readiness record, keyed by asset, version and card hash.

Binding to an exact version and hash is what makes staleness expressible. If
readiness pointed at the asset, a later edit would silently inherit every
relation built on the older text, and the user would see a confirmed
relation whose stated reason no longer matches what the card says.
KnowledgeCardReadinessRecordV1.title: KnowledgeCardReadinessRecordV1

LedgerStatementV1.description: One material statement with explicit provenance and evidence status.
LedgerStatementV1.title: LedgerStatementV1

M1IngestRequestV1.description: One bounded text source submitted to start an Experience Asset.
M1IngestRequestV1.title: M1IngestRequestV1

M1ProgressV1.description: Truthful M1 progress without a fabricated percentage or ETA.
M1ProgressV1.title: M1ProgressV1

M3CreateRequestV1.description: Start M3 only from one exact accepted M2/canonical pair.
M3CreateRequestV1.title: M3CreateRequestV1

M3EvidenceMomentV1.description: Readable, stable M2 evidence exposed for ledger review.
M3EvidenceMomentV1.title: M3EvidenceMomentV1

M3EvidenceStatementV1.description: Readable canonical statement plus human-facing source labels.
M3EvidenceStatementV1.title: M3EvidenceStatementV1

M3FailureV1.description: Stable public failure contract without raw prompt/tool/private payloads.
M3FailureV1.title: M3FailureV1

M3ProgressV1.description: State-derived progress; it never invents a percentage or ETA.
M3ProgressV1.title: M3ProgressV1

M3RegenerateRequestV1.description: Regenerate with CAS against the exact invalidated ledger shown to the user.
M3RegenerateRequestV1.title: M3RegenerateRequestV1

M4AcceptRequestV1.description:
Explicit acceptance of the map.

Acceptance is the only declared source of readiness. A weaker trigger — for
instance treating "no unresolved questions" as agreement — would attach
readiness to a card the user never said was finished, and every downstream
relation inherits that binding.
M4AcceptRequestV1.title: M4AcceptRequestV1

M4EvidenceStatementV1.description: Read-only projection of one canonical statement behind an insight.
M4EvidenceStatementV1.title: M4EvidenceStatementV1

M4WorkspaceV1.description:
Composed read model for the M4 workspace.

Evidence is included so the user can open what a lesson rests on. Without
the drill-down they can only accept or reject a lesson on its plausibility,
which is exactly the judgement the evidence exists to replace.
M4WorkspaceV1.title: M4WorkspaceV1

NotImplementedDetailV1.description: Body of a placeholder response, naming the ticket that will replace it.
NotImplementedDetailV1.title: NotImplementedDetailV1

ProjectionEdgeType.description:
Membership edges only.

Every edge means "this canonical record has this member in this role".
Statement order, temporal proximity and semantic similarity cannot prove
causation, so no edge asserts it; a causal label would present the system's
guess with the same authority as the user's own confirmed account.
ProjectionEdgeType.title: ProjectionEdgeType

ReadinessLifecycle.description:
Lifecycle of a readiness record.

Deliberately not `ProjectionLifecycle`: a projection is built incrementally
and only becomes eligible when complete, but readiness is minted whole by
one explicit user action. Reusing the projection enum let a readiness record
claim `CONFIRMED` while sitting in `BUILDING`, which two consumers could
reasonably read as opposite answers to "is this card ready".
ReadinessLifecycle.title: ReadinessLifecycle

RelatedCandidateDiscoveryArguments.description:
Cross-asset summary discovery.

There is deliberately no free-text query. A relation is meant to be a
durable statement about two assets, while a query is a one-off question:
driving discovery by phrasing lets the same pair yield different relations
under different wordings, so the relation degrades into what one sentence
returned once. The Runtime-owned `discovery_intent_version` removes that
variance — though reproducibility itself comes from the discovery
fingerprint and its idempotent cache, not from this field alone.

`top_k` is retained for interface compatibility and is a **ceiling, never a
quota**. Treating it as a quota would pressure the service into padding one
defensible candidate with weaker ones, and a weak relation costs more of the
user's attention than a missed one does.
RelatedCandidateDiscoveryArguments.title: RelatedCandidateDiscoveryArguments

RelationCandidateDecisionV1.description:
The user's explicit decision about one exact candidate.

Every binding the decision was made against is carried so that a request
arriving with a stale card version fails closed rather than being resolved
against whatever is current. Resolving it silently would grant access based
on a decision the user made about different content.
RelationCandidateDecisionV1.title: RelationCandidateDecisionV1

RelationCandidateV1.description:
A validated cross-asset candidate.

This replaces the pre-E5 fixture shape, which carried a free-text
`proposed_relation` and a flat provenance list and could not express a fixed
relation type, bilateral mapping, boundary nodes, projection bindings,
fingerprint or lifecycle. Extending it is a breaking change to a symbol the
E5→E6 handoff manifest freezes, and E6 needs the new shape before it lands.

`detail_included` is pinned false: the candidate view never carries
historical detail, because showing the detail before the decision would make
the confirmation choice moot.
RelationCandidateV1.title: RelationCandidateV1

RelationLifecycle.description:
Lifecycle of a validated candidate or a confirmed relation.

Records are append-only; invalidation moves state here rather than deleting
the row, because deleting it would make an invalidated relation
indistinguishable from one that never existed.
RelationLifecycle.title: RelationLifecycle

RelationNodeMappingV1.description:
One bilateral node correspondence proposed by the model.

The model returns only supplied node identifiers. It cannot return new
facts, nodes, edges, provenance, scores or titles, because the Runtime can
validate an identifier against a stored projection but cannot validate an
invented claim.

A role of `None` on both sides marks a root-to-root mapping, which is what
`SAME_THEME` claims. Roles must be absent or present together: a mapping
that pairs a root with a member describes a correspondence between things
of different kinds, and no relation type defines what that would mean.
RelationNodeMappingV1.title: RelationNodeMappingV1

RelationProvenanceRefV1.description:
Side-attributed provenance.

The side is explicit because a flat reference list cannot say which asset a
reference belongs to, and a bilateral explanation that cannot be attributed
to both sides is not bilateral.
RelationProvenanceRefV1.title: RelationProvenanceRefV1

RelationType.description:
Closed vocabulary for cross-asset relations.

The vocabulary is closed so a relation label means the same thing in a
session weeks later. A model-invented synonym would read as a distinct
relation to the user while carrying no admissibility rule behind it, so
abstention preserves meaning better than an unmapped label.
RelationType.title: RelationType

RelationWorkspaceV1.description:
Read-only composition of relation state for the API.

This is what replaces the retired snapshot fields for consumers. It is
composed on read and never serialized back into the Experience Asset
snapshot, so a relation read cannot change the snapshot JSON or its content
hash.
RelationWorkspaceV1.title: RelationWorkspaceV1

The outcome is one of six discriminated states. `NO_MATCH` is a semantic
claim and is cached; `TECHNICAL_FAILURE` is not, because caching an

post.description:
Start one summary-only discovery for an exact ready card.

Discovery runs only from an explicit user action. Before exact readiness
it is denied with a typed reason and performs no cross-asset read and no
model call — doing the read and discarding it would already have exposed
historical material to the model and spent the budget, so the denial has
to happen before the work rather than after.

post.description:
Read the deterministic bilateral evidence card for a confirmed relation.

The card is rendered by application code from canonical content, with no
second model call. A generated summary would be a new artifact produced
after the confirmation gate — never reviewed by the user, free to drift
from the relation they approved, and reading as a faithful description
of it.
